question: What are ways to improve the behavior of the grating couplers?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies apodization—individually tuning the length/width of each grating tooth, starting from a simple fully-etched grating structure—as a primary design strategy for high-efficiency grating couplers.
examples: Each grating's width is separately tuned to maximize overall coupling efficiency
Tuning each grating period's fill factor starting from a fully etched structure

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that apodized designs are obtained computationally via gradient-based numerical algorithms (with least-squares discretization) that fully automate the 1D grating coupler design.
examples: General gradient-based 1D grating design algorithm automates the design process
Least-squares discretization enables fully automated coupler optimization achieving <0.2 dB insertion loss

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer describes exploiting topologically enabled unidirectional guided resonances—resonances that cannot radiate downward but still radiate upward—as a route to low-loss grating couplers for on/off-chip coupling.
examples: UGRs in photonic crystal slabs enabled by topological charges serve as low-loss couplers
Downward radiation is suppressed while up-down symmetry breaking preserves top-side radiation

ingredients.name: answer_critical_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer states that adding a bottom reflector (distributed Bragg mirror or metal mirror) recovers power otherwise lost to downward radiation into the substrate, improving coupling efficiency.
examples: A bottom DBR mirror redirects substrate-bound light back toward the fiber
Metal mirrors under the grating reduce substrate loss and boost efficiency

ingredients.name: answer_critical_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer mentions index engineering of the layers above the grating—via thin-film overlays or vertically stacked dual-layer gratings—to reshape the mode profile and diffraction properties for better fiber coupling.
examples: An additional thin-film overlay reshapes the coupler mode profile
Dual-layer gratings stacked in the vertical direction modify diffraction behavior

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer explains the topological mechanism: an integer topological charge of a BIC splits into half-integer charges that evolve in momentum space, recombine, and render the far-field polarization undefined, thereby forbidding downward radiation while upward radiation persists.
examples: Half-integer charges bounce into each other and act as an integer charge again
Breaking up-down mirror symmetry lets the resonance still radiate upward, unlike traditional BICs

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer motivates the improvements via the fiber-to-waveguide mode-area mismatch (≈80 μm² fiber vs <0.2 μm² SOI waveguide) or grating couplers' placement flexibility for wafer-level testing, and notes trade-offs such as ease of fabrication versus computational cost or comparison with edge coupling.
examples: Edge coupling offers <0.5 dB loss over >100 nm but requires facet polishing and high-resolution alignment
Apodized designs are easy to fabricate but computationally intensive

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer notes that optimized grating designs can also achieve supplementary functionalities, such as polarization insensitivity, wavelength demultiplexing, or sub-0.2 dB single-wavelength couplers.
examples: The optimization algorithm designed polarization-insensitive and wavelength-demultiplexing gratings
A single-wavelength grating coupler with under 0.2 dB insertion loss was demonstrated
